item.title: PHP cURL POST Requests: Handling Empty POST Data with JSON Payloads
item.description:
“PHP cURL POST Requests: Handling Empty POST Data with JSON Payloads”

How can we correctly transmit and receive JSON data via cURL when the server-side script is encountering an empty $_POST?

Server-Side: Reading Raw JSON Input

If your receiving web server expects data formatted as JSON, you must explicitly read the raw request body instead of relying on $_POST.

The accepted approach involves fetching the request stream content directly:

$rawJsonData = file_get_contents('php://input');
$dataObject = json_decode($rawJsonData);

This snippet reads everything sent in the body of the HTTP request and decodes it into a PHP object or array.

item.title: PHP cURL SSL Verification Error: Solutions for 'failed loading cafile'
item.description:
“PHP cURL SSL Verification Error: Solutions for ‘failed loading cafile’”

Encountering a “failed loading cafile” error with PHP’s cURL extension can halt your network requests. This typically means cURL cannot locate or verify the SSL certificate authority (CA) bundle required to establish a secure HTTPS connection. This issue commonly arises in local development environments like WAMP or XAMPP where the certificate store might be misconfigured or missing.

Several effective methods exist to resolve this, ranging from configuring php.ini to temporarily disabling verification (with caveats). Let’s explore these solutions.

item.title: PHP cURL: Debugging with Verbose Output and Request Metrics
item.description:
“PHP cURL: Debugging with Verbose Output and Request Metrics”

When working with PHP cURL, obtaining detailed information about a request can be crucial for troubleshooting. This involves leveraging specific cURL options to log verbose output and retrieve performance metrics. Here’s a breakdown of various methods to achieve this.

Solution 1: Utilizing CURLOPT_VERBOSE and CURLOPT_STDERR for Detailed Logging

A primary method for debugging cURL requests in PHP is by enabling the CURLOPT_VERBOSE option. This flag instructs cURL to output detailed information about the transfer process. This output is typically directed to standard error (STDERR). You can redirect this output to a temporary stream for later examination.
